items.title: Jon-Erik Kellso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: getting into the Eddie Condon group with Bobby Hackett and Wild Bill Davison

ctx.x: What was happening with your personal tastes as far as the kinds of jazz you were listening to?

Good question. I’ve been through a lot of phases, I guess you could say. My first listening experiences were Swing Era, then I started sort of going backwards from there and learning about and listening to Bix Beiderbecke and Louis Armstrong, and also then getting into the Eddie Condon group with Bobby Hackett and Wild Bill Davison. And I kind of, I sort of jumped a little bit and then my dad had one Miles Davis record and I listened to that and I thought wow, this is just a completely different way to play the…

buy one record, looking for one particular guy, and then somebody else on that record opens your eyes and you say now I’ve got to get this guy’s records. So I went through, in high school I started to go through a period where I was buying a lot of bebop records. I liked that too. And I started to play a little bit of the groups that were kind of trying to play that style. And of course the college jazz programs generally aren’t really geared towards the older styles of music. They’re generally bebop and beyond,…
